problem_text:
A manufacturing consortium aims to devise a resource‑conservation strategy to curtail raw‑material waste from several production lines. Initially, no waste‑reduction practices are in place.

The characteristics of each production line are as follows:
* For Line 1, waste coefficient is 0.616, output is 93.462.
* For Line 2, waste coefficient is 2.951, output is 213.419.
* For Line 3, waste coefficient is 1.31, output is 141.324.
* For Line 4, waste coefficient is 2.259, output is 213.334.
* For Line 5, waste coefficient is 1.803, output is 258.867.
* For Line 6, waste coefficient is 2.574, output is 179.166.
* For Line 7, waste coefficient is 2.587, output is 144.082.
* For Line 8, waste coefficient is 1.158, output is 276.811.
* For Line 9, waste coefficient is 1.861, output is 179.093.

To mitigate waste, several recycling technologies are available, each characterized by a specific recovery rate:
* By adopting Technology 1, material loss will be lowered by 62%.
* By adopting Technology 2, material loss will be lowered by 21%.
* By adopting Technology 3, material loss will be lowered by 51%.
* By adopting Technology 4, material loss will be lowered by 51%.
* By adopting Technology 5, material loss will be lowered by 42%.
* By adopting Technology 6, material loss will be lowered by 50%.
* By adopting Technology 7, material loss will be lowered by 79%.
* By adopting Technology 8, material loss will be lowered by 77%.
* By adopting Technology 9, material loss will be lowered by 84%.

Implementing a technology on a production line incurs an extra expense per unit of output. The expense matrix for all line–technology pairings is summarized below:

| Line \ Technology | Tech 1 | Tech 2 | Tech 3 | Tech 4 | Tech 5 | Tech 6 | Tech 7 | Tech 8 | Tech 9 |
|------------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Line 1           | 132.261| 50.188 | 45.512 | 78.822 | 146.288| 32.483 | 53.766 | 164.123| 146.849|
| Line 2           | 101.488| 100.975| 50.034 | 40.637 | 168.339| 14.265 | 18.197 | 118.962| 40.615 |
| Line 3           | 129.613| 17.446 | 118.731| 20.623 | 59.069 | 44.207 | 192.065| 123.878| 117.085|
| Line 4           | 13.538 | 146.714| 135.732| 63.856 | 26.292 | 95.349 | 198.627| 174.787| 42.408 |
| Line 5           | 167.769| 124.159| 160.977| 165.886| 44.558 | 135.333| 60.259 | 147.595| 75.108 |
| Line 6           | 96.159 | 122.213| 53.665 | 83.238 | 30.628 | 48.446 | 173.322| 105.828| 89.761 |
| Line 7           | 38.417 | 28.297 | 100.415| 126.802| 17.417 | 158.935| 105.633| 32.328 | 101.626|
| Line 8           | 34.762 | 124.66 | 167.229| 180.424| 157.225| 133.354| 109.188| 80.372 | 18.253 |
| Line 9           | 110.665| 53.602 | 162.437| 160.016| 82.435 | 121.919| 150.865| 154.692| 142.374|

The consortium must decide which technologies to deploy on each line (lines may employ multiple technologies concurrently), and a line may also remain partially untreated if needed.
The objective is to guarantee that the total raw‑material waste is decreased by at least a fraction P = 0.249 of the baseline waste, while minimizing the overall implementation cost.
